title: Space optimization

overview.what: If `dp[i]`'s transition only reads a FIXED small window of previous states, you don't need to keep the whole table. A few rolling variables or rows will suffice.
overview.why: It reduces the space complexity of bottom-up DP significantly. A 1D array collapses from O(n) space to O(1) space, and a 2D matrix collapses from O(m*n) to O(n) space.

why_learning_this: In an interview, coming up with the O(n) space DP is the pass. Reducing it to O(1) space is the strong hire.
Space-optimized DP is often used in real memory-constrained environments where allocating a huge matrix is impossible.

common_mistakes.title: Applying it blindly to unbounded lookbacks
common_mistakes.explanation: If `dp[i]` depends on a value arbitrarily far back in the table (like in Longest Increasing Subsequence, where `dp[i]` checks every `j < i`), you cannot collapse it to a fixed window. It only works if the lookback distance is a constant.

common_mistakes.title: Losing the ability to reconstruct the path
common_mistakes.explanation: When you space-optimize, you throw away older states. You only retain the numeric answer. If the problem asks you to return the actual path (e.g. which items were selected), you cannot space-optimize without extra bookkeeping.

recall_questions.q: What is the generalizable rule for when you can space-optimize a DP table?
recall_questions.answer: You can optimize space if the recurrence depends only on a fixed, constant window of previous states (like just `i-1` and `i-2`, or just the previous row).

recall_questions.q: What is the primary trade-off of space optimization?
recall_questions.answer: You lose the ability to reconstruct the actual solution path (e.g., which items were chosen), as the older states needed for backtracking are discarded.

recall_questions.q: How does a 2D grid DP table (like unique paths) space-optimize?
recall_questions.answer: If `dp[i][j]` only depends on the current row and the row above it (`i-1`), the entire `m * n` matrix can be collapsed to just two `n`-length rows, dropping space from O(m*n) to O(n).

practice_tasks.title: Analyze space optimization applicability
practice_tasks.prompt: Look at this recurrence: `dp[i] = dp[i-1] + max(dp[0...i-2])`. Can you space-optimize this to O(1) variables?
practice_tasks.solution: No, because computing `dp[i]` requires looking at potentially *all* previous states `dp[0...i-2]`, not just a fixed window. You must keep the full array.

understanding_checks.question: A DP algorithm uses a 1D array where `dp[i]` is computed using only `dp[i-1]`, `dp[i-2]`, and `dp[i-3]`. What is the minimum space complexity we can achieve?
understanding_checks.why: The transition only looks back 3 steps. We can maintain 3 rolling variables instead of an array of size `n`. 3 variables is a constant, hence O(1) space.

understanding_checks.question: A developer space-optimizes a knapsack DP to one row, but iterates left-to-right. Why does this give the wrong answer for 0/1 knapsack?
understanding_checks.answer: Iterating left-to-right overwrites the row with current-item data, so cells later in the row read values that ALREADY include the current item.
understanding_checks.why: 0/1 knapsack requires the item to be used at most once. By scanning right-to-left, we ensure we only read the PREVIOUS item's state before we overwrite it.
